title: Naqvi Carries Special Letter from Field Marshal Munir to Khamenei in Third Tehran Visit
detail: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran on June 6-7 carrying a special message from Field Marshal Asim Munir addressed to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Naqvi met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and other senior officials to present new Pakistani proposals for a temporary US-Iran deal, aiming to revive formal peace negotiations. The visit coincided with US forces downing Iranian drones over the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring the active conflict context. Pakistan's sustained mediation effort — Naqvi's third Iran visit in recent weeks — reflects Islamabad's deepening role as a key intermediary, leveraging its ties with both Washington and Tehran.

title: Gilgit-Baltistan Legislative Assembly Elections Held; PTI Forced to Compete as Independents
detail: Pakistan held general elections for the 33-seat Gilgit-Baltistan Legislative Assembly on June 7, 2026, with 130 party candidates and 266 independents contesting 24 general seats. The Election Commission barred PTI from using its official party symbol — upheld by the Supreme Court under the same formula as the February 2024 national elections — forcing its candidates to run as independents. The party alleged a 'lack of level playing field,' with leaders expelled from GB in the days prior and workers reportedly detained. Polling ran from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. under tight security, with vote counting underway by end of day. The elections are seen as a key test of political sentiment in the strategic northern territory.

media.caption: Gilgit-Baltistan Legislative Assembly elections, June 7, 2026 — PTI forced to compete as independents
